answer: A public place that was recently renovated in my town is the riverside walkway along the Jamuna, which has been beautifully transformed over the last couple of years. It runs along the embankment on the edge of Sirajganj, not far from where I live. It used to be quite neglected and run-down, with broken paving, rubbish piling up and hardly any lights, so most people avoided it after dark, and the change has been remarkable. Now it features a wide walking path, proper lighting, rows of young trees and plenty of seating, making it far more [[accessible]] to everyone, including elderly people and families with small children. The whole area feels clean, modern and genuinely [[welcoming]], which it never did before. On any given evening it is now full of people walking, jogging or simply relaxing by the water, and a few tea stalls have opened nearby. What I appreciate most is how the renovation has [[revitalised]] a part of the town that was previously ignored. It has become a real gathering point for the community, and I often bump into neighbours and old classmates there. My parents now walk there most evenings, which is good for my father now that he has retired. Honestly, I think this kind of investment in public spaces is [[commendable]], because it improves everyone's quality of life. My only concern is that it must be properly maintained, or it could [[fall into disrepair]] again. It has quickly become one of my favourite places to unwind, and it shows what good urban planning can achieve.

followUps.q: Do you think more public places should be improved?
followUps.answer: Definitely. There are several parks and fields in our town that are in poor condition, and improving them would benefit everyone, especially children and elderly people who have few other places to go.

followUps.q: Who should pay for improvements like this?
followUps.answer: Mainly the local government, as it is a public space. But I think local businesses could also contribute, because a pleasant area attracts more visitors, which is good for their trade as well.

note: 'My city' changed to his town by the Jamuna; added what it was like before, who uses it (retired father), maintenance concern; added mark 'fall into disrepair'.
